title: Accessibility Services, U of T
context: Professional work / Research & design; not implemented
description: Making course accommodations easier to manage for students, instructors, and Accessibility Services staff.
contribution: Led student and instructor interviews, explored workflows, and designed accommodation interfaces for ACORN and CIS.
evidence: Two rounds of interviews with each user group informed the designs. The project did not proceed to implementation; no post-launch outcomes were measured.

title: Design System: Cards
description: Supporting simple content and complex interactions with a consistent, reusable card component.
contribution: Researched existing patterns, designed Basic and Instance-Swap variants, documented behavior, and reviewed implementation with a developer.
evidence: Designer feedback informed a reusable header. Implementation review covered visual specifications, keyboard navigation, and screen-reader behavior.

title: StitchFit
description: Helping online shoppers navigate inconsistent clothing sizes and find a fit that suits them.
contribution: Conducted user research, explored sizing concepts, and iterated on onboarding and shopping flows through usability testing.
evidence: Five research interviews, three low-fidelity tests, and five high-fidelity usability tests informed the prototype. AI sizing accuracy was not validated.

title: Info Security Website, U of T
description: Bringing fragmented security resources from three University of Toronto websites into one clear destination.
contribution: Audited content, mapped information architecture, designed audience-based navigation, and documented interface patterns.
evidence: A hybrid card sort with 14 security team members informed the structure. Two legacy websites were decommissioned following consolidation.

title: Lore Magazine
description: Giving a Toronto-based independent magazine a visual identity that supports diverse community stories.
contribution: Art direction, graphic design, and production for a collaborative editorial publication.
evidence: The case study presents published issues and the visual direction developed for the magazine.

title: Basement Boutiq Studio
description: Building a cohesive brand and product collection for a handmade accessories business.
contribution: Designed the brand, jewellery, keychains, and stickers, alongside an online shop and market presence.
evidence: A collection of physical products, packaging, and shop materials shows the brand across digital and in-person touchpoints.

title: 3D Character and Brand Design
description: Connecting a refreshed brand identity with a zodiac-inspired toy collection.
contribution: Redesigned the logo and explored characters through 2D artwork, 3D models, and product mockups.
evidence: Deliverables include identity explorations, toy models, and concepts for web and print.

title: Architecture Projects
description: Exploring how mapping, representation, and spatial design can reveal new possibilities for urban places.
contribution: Developed architectural proposals, maps, drawings, and models across a collection of projects.
evidence: The selected work documents design exploration and representation; proposals are not presented as built outcomes.
